title: Wing Leading Edge Harnesses — Anti-Ice Valve and Slat Position Feeds
abstract: Wiring diagram for the left wing fixed leading edge, covering the anti-ice valve control and feedback runs, the slat position sensing feeds and the harness supports that share brackets with the piccolo ducts.

sections.purpose: This sheet gives the wiring of the left wing fixed leading edge, from the wing junction disconnect outboard to the anti-ice valves and the slat position sensing installation.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet is drawn looking forward with the slats extended. The important feature is the shared support: from rib 12 outboard the harness brackets pick up the same rib holes as the piccolo duct supports, so any change to the duct support arrangement moves the harness as well. The clamp positions in the table are dimensioned from the outboard flange of the sliding duct support at each rib. The right wing is on the companion sheet with mirrored rib numbering.
sections.routing_note: The harness leaves the wing junction disconnect, runs outboard along the front spar at mid height and branches to each anti-ice valve position. From rib 12 outboard it shares brackets with the piccolo duct supports and is clamped at the dimensions in the sheet table, taken from the sliding support flange. The slat position sensing feeds break out at rib 8 and run in a separate protected loom.

title: Wing Leading Edge Harnesses — Anti-Ice Valve and Slat Position Feeds

issue.reason: Clamp position references given separately for the sliding support and for the bellows-compensated foot, whose flange the earlier dimensions no longer reach.

abstract: Wiring diagram for the left wing fixed leading edge, covering the anti-ice valve control and feedback runs, the slat position sensing feeds and the harness supports that share brackets with the piccolo ducts.

sections.purpose: This sheet gives the wiring of the left wing fixed leading edge, from the wing junction disconnect outboard to the anti-ice valves and the slat position sensing installation.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet is drawn looking forward with the slats extended. The important feature is the shared support: from rib 12 outboard the harness brackets pick up the same rib holes as the piccolo duct supports, so any change to the duct support arrangement moves the harness as well. The clamp position table is now in two columns. Column A is dimensioned from the outboard flange of the sliding duct support and applies to a pre MOD-163208 wing. Column B is dimensioned from the inboard collar of the bellows-compensated fixed foot and applies to a post MOD-163208 wing; the sliding flange the column A dimensions are taken from does not exist on that wing, and a clamp set to a column A figure there sits about 18 mm outboard of where it belongs and loads the branch at the anti-ice valve. Where a duct support has been replaced, reclamp to column B and check the position against this sheet before the leading edge is closed. The right wing is on the companion sheet with mirrored rib numbering.
sections.routing_note: The harness leaves the wing junction disconnect, runs outboard along the front spar at mid height and branches to each anti-ice valve position. From rib 12 outboard it shares brackets with the piccolo duct supports and is clamped at the dimensions in the sheet table; read column A on a sliding support and column B on a bellows-compensated foot. The slat position sensing feeds break out at rib 8 and run in a separate protected loom, which is unaffected by the support change.
